implementerProof.how: Re-driven whole at this head rather than carried, which is what the merge made necessary and what the implementer itself recommended (Envoy 64769c016c64ef6b7d05b46b87909536, naming the rows its merge made stale: the durable names moved into the bus package, and the consumer reconciliation's lease split per durable). Driven here: the whole two-process package (ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/cmd/dispatch 309.419s, every row), the duty package (ok 6.078s), the api gate rows twice (ok 24.244s), the docs race and evictor rows eight consecutive times (ok 41.546s), the browser suite (83 passed, 4 skipped, 6.2m), and two surfaces of my own below. proof.criterion: The review's important finding 1, and the correction to my own round-1 evidence: a reader whose connection ends because the event log was reset beneath it is live again when the browser reconnects with the last id it saw — which is above the new log's head, since the browser only ever raises it.
proof.surface: Two real envoy-dispatch processes on one Postgres 17 and one nats-server 2.10 in this issue's pod; GET /api/v1/events held open on process A, the log reset with `truncate table events restart identity cascade` beneath it, and the reconnect made with ?since=<the id the reader last saw>, which is what a browser's Last-Event-ID sends.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && . /legion/harness/env.sh && go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -timeout 30m -run TestProbeAReaderResumingAfterAResetWithItsOldLastEventIDIsLiveAgain ./cmd/dispatch   (throwaway probe, removed before this handoff)
proof.observed: The reader saw the log to id 6 and its stream ended at the reset, as the relay intends. It resumed at since=6, above the refilled log's head, and received the next issue B created — live, on the resumed connection. My round-1 probe reconnected with no since at all, which no browser does, so it passed on a connection a real reader never opens; this is that measurement corrected.
proof.negativeControl: Driven, not argued: on a scratch clone of this head with the clamp reverted to its pre-review form (`if !sinceProvided` alone, so a resuming client's since is no longer held to the head) and nothing else changed, the same probe fails — `the stream never carried issue.created RS6VH2M0X-7 within 30s` — which is the reader silent for good on an open, heartbeating connection that the review described.

proof.criterion: Contract change census, entry 1: the one refusal a person meets, `docs.ErrRoomBehindHead` on the browser's own update over /ws/doc/{room}, driven through the client that builds the input rather than argued from the mapping.
proof.surface: Two real envoy-dispatch processes with a document websocket client attached to the room on A. The room was held resident and behind on purpose rather than raced for: every backend holding the `dispatch_doc_changed` LISTEN was terminated across B's write (`pg_terminate_backend`), and nothing catches up a notification missed that way (docs/stale_room.go), so A kept a room the store had moved past. Then the browser typed.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && . /legion/harness/env.sh && go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -timeout 30m -run TestProbeABrowserAppendFromARoomBehindTheHeadIsRefused ./cmd/dispatch   (throwaway probe, removed before this handoff)
proof.observed: A refused the append and said exactly what it refused: `ygo/websocket: StoreUpdate for room "58e741d7-…": document service unavailable: the document's room is behind its durable head: room 58e741d7-… holds the document through update 2, the stored document stands at 3`. The room then failed and reloaded, and both processes served the document the store holds ("after"). No edit was lost and nothing was written from the stale room.
proof.negativeControl: The refusal is the deliberately broken input here — a write made from a document state this process does not hold — and what it is controlled against is the same write with the room current: sixteen concurrent cross-process edits through POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits refused none, three rounds running, because a route's write forks from the store instead (forkLive). That measurement is also what corrected the census: its earlier draft listed six API route families as newly able to answer 503 for this reason, which is not what the code does; the implementer replaced that table with the three appends that carry a room cursor after I asked it to name the route I should drive (Envoy c516485aa6e7176e04867b2ab8662a02). I record the earlier version as the error it was; the table now on the pull request matches what I measured.

proof.criterion: The merge's own second change: the consumer reconciliation's lease is one per durable, so a reconciliation stuck on one durable cannot keep the other's intake from ever creating its own.
proof.surface: Two real envoy-dispatch processes against one nats-server with JetStream, read from the processes' own logs and NATS's ConsumerInfo.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && . /legion/harness/env.sh && go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -timeout 30m -run TestProbeBothDurablesBindUnderThePerDurableLease ./cmd/dispatch   (throwaway probe, removed before this handoff)
proof.observed: Both durables bound, the other process standing by for each with no `level=ERROR dispatch delivery:` line. The leases are now per durable and each reported once per process: `delivery-consumer-delivery-events` and `delivery-consumer-delivery-jobs`, with the old single `delivery-consumers` lease reported nowhere.
proof.negativeControl: The row fails if either durable is bound by both processes, if a standby logs the refusal at ERROR, or if the superseded single-lease name appears at all. The failure the split answers is main's own live row (`without the delivery consumer create Dispatch leaves only that intake unbound`), which needs Docker and runs in CI, green at the merge head; the implementer drove it here against a real nats-server with that one create denied, recorded in its handoff.

notes: The open question of five rounds is answered, by the reviewer rather than by me: the required set on main is lint, typecheck, test and pr-title, read from the rulesets (.legion/INFRA-66/review.json, ciReadAtTheCodeHead). So dispatch-multiprocess is NOT required, and a red two-process run would not block a merge. The three red tests my earlier rounds added are all in lanes that are required or in packages those lanes run — duty and api are envoy-go's — so each of them would have held a merge; the two-process rows would not. That is worth an operator's attention after this merges, not a finding against this change.

The census's earlier draft was wrong and I am recording it rather than only its correction: it listed six API route families as newly able to answer 503 for ErrRoomBehindHead. The code forks from the store instead on those routes, which my sixteen-edit measurement showed three rounds running, and the implementer replaced the table with the three appends that carry a room cursor when I asked which route to drive. The table now on the pull request matches what I measured.

Two bounds of the period gate named in round 5 are unchanged and still true at this head — one ungated pass at a change of period, and one pass per aligned period rather than per arbitrary window — and the third, the nanosecond scale equality, is unchanged. All three are in migration 0115's own comment.
Not driven here, and named rather than implied: internal/dispatch/delivery's own tests and envoy-infra's live row need Docker, which this pod has not got. Both are green in CI at the merge head.

Production: nothing deploys Dispatch automatically (dispatch://INFRA-64), so the production check after the merge will be a record of which build production runs and that it does not yet carry the merge, as dispatch://INFRA-62's was.
